title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 51 (Payment of Dividend in Proportion to Amount Paid-Up)

content.overview: Section 51 provides that a company may, if so authorised by its articles, pay dividends in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share where a larger amount is paid up on some shares than on others.
content.glance: If articles authorise, dividends may be paid in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share where paid-up amounts differ.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 51 (Payment of Dividend in Proportion to Amount Paid-Up). Section 51 provides that a company may, if so authorised by its articles, pay dividends in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share where a larger amount is paid up on some shares than on others. State the trigger, the person who must comply, and the consequence in the section. A related section is a cross-reference, not a substitute for this rule. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Articles Authority
sections.body: Proportional dividend is available only if the articles authorise it.

sections.heading: Proportion to Paid-Up
sections.body: Where some shares have a larger amount paid up than others, dividend may be paid in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share.

provisions.title: Payment of dividend in proportion to amount paid-up

examples.title: Proportional dividend
examples.body: Articles authorise proportional dividend. Shares with ₹50 paid-up receive half the dividend per share of fully paid ₹100 shares. Section 51 is applied.

examples.title: No articles authority
examples.body: Articles are silent. The company cannot rely on s. 51 to pay dividend only in proportion to paid-up amounts without articles authorisation.

hypotheticals.question: Must dividends always be proportional to paid-up capital?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only if the articles authorise it under s. 51. Otherwise the company’s dividend distribution follows the articles and general dividend rules.

distinctions.title: Proportional dividend (s. 51) vs acceptance of unpaid capital (s. 50)
distinctions.left: How dividend is calculated on partly paid shares
distinctions.right: Power to accept uncalled capital in advance

misconceptions.trap: Partly paid shareholders always get reduced dividend by force of statute alone.
misconceptions.correction: Section 51 applies only if the articles authorise proportional dividend.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 51 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Check articles. II. Compare paid-up amounts. III. Apply proportional rule if authorised. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Articles; paid-up amounts; dividend calculation; precise relief.

examTips: Proportion is to amount paid-up, not nominal value alone.
